options.text: Entry, exit, stop and size are defined exactly
options.explanation: Right: then anyone applying it to the same chart makes the same trades.

options.text: It uses at least one indicator
options.explanation: No: an indicator can still be read by feel.

options.text: It has made money in a backtest before
options.explanation: No: results say nothing about whether the rules are exact.

questions.prompt: Average 1.3500 now, 1.3420 ten candles ago; latest close 1.3460. What do the simplified trend rules allow?

options.text: A long, because the average is rising
options.explanation: No: a long also needs a close above the average, and 1.3460 is below 1.3500.

options.text: No entry: below a rising average
options.explanation: Right: a long needs a close above a rising average; a short needs a close below a falling one. Neither holds.

options.text: A short, because the close is below the average
options.explanation: No: a short also needs a falling average, and this one rose from 1.3420.

questions.prompt: A long fills at 1.0850 with ATR 0.0025. Where is a 2 × ATR stop?

options.explanation: No: that is 1 × ATR. The rule uses 2 × 0.0025 = 0.0050.
No: a long's stop is below the entry.

questions.prompt: Previous 20 candles' high 1.2740, low 1.2610. Today's high is 1.2755 but it closes at 1.2735. Is there a long signal?

options.text: No: the close is inside the channel
options.explanation: Right: the rules use closes, and 1.2735 is below 1.2740.
No: an intraday spike that closes inside the channel is not a signal.
No: these simplified rules have no volume condition; the close decides.

questions.prompt: You compared 8 lookbacks on the same years and kept the best. What should you do next?

options.text: Use it at once, as it was the best
options.explanation: No: the best of several settings on one data set usually flatters the result.

options.text: Test it on data you did not use to choose it
options.explanation: Right: an out-of-sample check shows how much of the result was fitted to noise.

options.text: Keep adjusting it until every year is positive
options.explanation: No: tuning until everything looks good is overfitting.

questions.prompt: Why does this module teach generic versions rather than named traders' systems?

options.text: Named systems are known to have stopped working
options.explanation: No: the module makes no claim about how any named system performs.

options.text: Generic versions are proven to work better
options.explanation: No: nothing here is proven to work; the versions are for learning and testing.

options.text: Named versions need a person to check their sources first
options.explanation: Right: attributions, rules and results for named traders are added only after human review against reliable sources.
